t: Napoleon pretended to be weak, gave up the Pratzen Heights and thinned his right flank, so that the Allies weakened their own centre to attack it; Soult's corps then took the Heights.
Davout's III Corps marched 110 km in 48 hours from Vienna to hold the French right against a much larger force.
Figures differ: one account gives the Allied army as 85,000 and the French as 72,000, another 89,000 and 66,000, and the Allied losses are given as about 36,000 against about 9,000 French.
dyk: Napoleon's letter to Joséphine spoke of a victory over the army commanded by 'the two emperors', which gave the battle its name of the Battle of the Three Emperors, though Emperor Francis of Austria was not present on the field.
ev: 200,000 French troops begin to cross the Rhine on a front of 260 km
Vienna falls, and Napoleon sets a trap by seeming weak and abandoning the Pratzen Heights
The Allied council adopts Weyrother’s plan, and Napoleon hides his troops behind the Bosenitz stream
The French take the Pratzen Heights and break the Allied centre, and the Allied army abandons the field
France and Austria sign a truce on 4 December
The Treaty of Pressburg takes Austria out of the war on 26 December

f.place: About ten kilometres south-east of Brno, between Brno and Austerlitz (Slavkov u Brna), then in the Austrian Empire, now in the Czech Republic
f.sides: The French Empire's Grande Armée under Napoleon I, some 72,000 men and 157 guns on one account; the Allied army under Tsar Alexander I and General Kutuzov with Austrian forces under Emperor Francis II, about 85,000 men and 318 guns on the same account
f.outcome: The French broke the Allied centre and routed the Allied army, taking thousands of prisoners. France and Austria agreed a truce on 4 December and signed the Treaty of Pressburg on 26 December.
